newsitem.title: CUBA: Castro says Cuban sugar harvest below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Castro says Cuban sugar harvest below expectations.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro said he does not believe Cuba's sugar harvest this year will reach the 4.45 million tonnes achieved in 1995/96.
"In my opinion, the harvest will not reach the same quantity as last year," Castro told Cuban reporters Thursday night after a May 1 ceremony in which outstanding workers received decorations.
His comments were broadcast by state-run Radio Rebelde Friday.

The Cuban president blamed this year's sugar harvest problems on Hurricane Lili which battered west and central provinces last October, damaging canefields, and on a tightening of the U.S. economic embargo which delayed the arrival of essential sugar harvest financing and inputs.
Castro offered no forecast for this year's harvest, which is still continuing, although harvesting is extending beyond the end-April optimum completion date.
Senior Cuban officials had been insisting that this year's harvest, despite the difficulties, would produce a "modest increase" over last year's crop.
Analysts said the Communist-ruled island urgently needs a good crop to meet sugar delivery commitments and pay back harvest pre-financing loans.
Castro said the economy was neverthless performing quite well this year, although the harvest was a negative factor.
But he urged the sugar sector to make the best possible use of its resources to prepare for the coming 1997/98 crop and said extra mobilizations of workers were needed.
